rockville-centre.title: Diocese of Rockville Centre (NY)
rockville-centre.narrative: The Diocese of Rockville Centre filed for Chapter 11 protection in October 2020, citing the financial pressure of over 200 lawsuits filed under the New York Child Victims Act. This filing halted all pending litigation and forced survivors into a centralized bankruptcy process. The case has been marked by contentious disputes over insurance coverage and the valuation of diocesan assets. In December 2024, a reorganization plan was confirmed, establishing a $323 million trust for survivors. Critics argue that the diocese used the bankruptcy process to shield significant assets held in separate 'parish corporations' and to avoid full transparency regarding the extent of abuse.
keyTactics: Aggressive use of the 'Corporation Sole' defense to shield parish assets.
Protracted litigation over insurance coverage to delay settlements.
Threats of 'Cramdown' to force a lower settlement amount on survivors.

buffalo.title: Diocese of Buffalo (NY)
buffalo.narrative: Facing a deluge of lawsuits under the Child Victims Act and a RICO lawsuit alleging a systemic cover-up, the Diocese of Buffalo filed for bankruptcy in February 2020. The filing came amidst a scandal involving Bishop Richard Malone. The bankruptcy process has been slow, with the diocese accused of low-balling settlement offers. A reorganization plan was confirmed in January 2025 with a $273.9M total fund. Internal audit documents revealed a 'progressive percentage' tax on parishes to fund the settlement, proving central financial control.
keyTactics: Filing for bankruptcy to halt RICO litigation and discovery.
Implementation of 'SJIF CVA Tax' accounts (2995/2996) to tax parishes.
Minimizing the value of real estate assets to reduce the settlement pool.

syracuse.title: Diocese of Syracuse (NY)
syracuse.narrative: Filed June 2020. Emerged from bankruptcy in Feb 2026 with a $176.1M settlement after a six-year process. The plan includes contributions from the diocese, parishes, and insurance carriers.
keyTactics: Six-year delay strategy.
Complex three-party contribution structure (Diocese, Parishes, Insurers).

rochester.title: Diocese of Rochester (NY)
rochester.narrative: The first NY diocese to file under the CVA window. Filed Sept 2019. Confirmed plan in 2022.
keyTactics: First-mover advantage in setting CVA precedents.

albany.title: Diocese of Albany (NY)
albany.narrative: Filed March 2023. Currently in mediation. Facing significant pressure from survivors to disclose assets.
keyTactics: Delaying discovery through mediation.

ogdensburg.title: Diocese of Ogdensburg (NY)
ogdensburg.narrative: Filed July 2023. Small rural diocese facing disproportionate liability.
keyTactics: Pleading poverty due to rural demographics.

san-francisco.title: Archdiocese of San Francisco (CA)
san-francisco.narrative: Filed in Aug 2023 to halt 500+ lawsuits. The Committee is fighting to declare parishes and schools as 'divisions' of the Archdiocese, not separate entities. Central assets were reported at $332.7M in 2021, but the Diocese claims much is restricted. Valuation of prime real estate is a key dispute.
keyTactics: Asserting parish/school assets are separate legal entities.
Undervaluing prime San Francisco real estate.
Using bankruptcy stay to delay trials.

oakland.title: Diocese of Oakland (CA)
oakland.narrative: Filed in May 2023. The Committee alleges the Diocese funneled $106M into the 'Oakland Parochial Fund' to shield assets. In Sept 2025, the Diocese moved to dismiss its own case, claiming professional fees ($37M) had 'bled the Debtor dry'. A&M managed the 'liquidity clock' to force a settlement or dismissal decision.
keyTactics: Funneling $106M to 'Oakland Parochial Fund' (OPF).
Threatening case dismissal when liquidity drops below $3M threshold.
Tapping Priest Retirement plans to pay professional fees.

sacramento.title: Diocese of Sacramento (CA)
sacramento.narrative: Filed April 2024 facing 250+ lawsuits. Reported $133.9M in assets. Mediation is ongoing, but insurers have challenged deals allowing test cases to proceed. Bishop Soto argued bankruptcy was the only 'equitable' path to prevent early plaintiffs from draining all assets.
keyTactics: Filing to prevent 'race to the courthouse' by early plaintiffs.
Leveraging insurance disputes to delay payouts.
Protecting $108.8M in unrestricted assets.

san-diego.title: Diocese of San Diego (CA)
san-diego.narrative: Filed June 2024 with ~450 claims. A federal judge ordered an external audit of 770 parish accounts after accusing the Diocese of 'hiding assets' and conspiring to create separate bank accounts. Reported $85.8M central assets.
keyTactics: Hiding assets in 770 separate parish accounts.
Conspiring to create separate bank accounts to evade creditors.
Claiming only $85.8M in central assets available.

fresno.title: Diocese of Fresno (CA)
fresno.narrative: Filed July 2025 with ~160 claims. Reported $50-100M in assets. The Diocese owes $30.3M to its own internal Deposit & Loan Fund, raising questions about asset commingling.
keyTactics: Commingling assets in Deposit & Loan Fund.

santa-rosa.title: Diocese of Santa Rosa (CA)
santa-rosa.narrative: Filed March 2023. Second time filing (first in 2004). Facing 200+ new claims.
keyTactics: Repeat filer strategy.

stockton.title: Diocese of Stockton (CA)
stockton.narrative: Filed Jan 2014. Concluded 2017. First CA diocese to file.
keyTactics: Setting CA precedent.

santa-fe.title: Archdiocese of Santa Fe (NM)
santa-fe.narrative: Filed Dec 2018. Settled for $121.5M in 2022. Major ruling on fraudulent conveyance regarding Catholic Peoples Foundation.
keyTactics: Attempted transfer of assets to Catholic Peoples Foundation.

gallup.title: Diocese of Gallup (NM)
gallup.narrative: Filed Nov 2013. Cross-border diocese (NM/AZ). Settled for $21M in 2016.
keyTactics: Managing cross-state jurisdiction issues.

baltimore.title: Archdiocese of Baltimore (MD)
baltimore.narrative: Filed in Sept 2023 facing ~922 survivor claims. The Archdiocese reported $204.9M in assets but offered only a $33.1M 'Catholic Family Contribution', which the Creditors Committee rejected as 'an insult'. The case is a major battleground over the valuation of assets and the 'Corporation Sole' defense, with survivors demanding nearly $1 billion.
keyTactics: Lowball 'Catholic Family Contribution' offer based on past voluntary settlements.
Shielding $163.9M in cash/investments from the estate.
Aggressive litigation to prevent piercing the corporate veil.

new-orleans.title: Archdiocese of New Orleans (LA)
new-orleans.narrative: Filed in May 2020 to stop the deposition of Archbishop Aymond. The case has been highly controversial due to the high 'burn rate' of professional fees and the transfer of assets to new trusts prior to filing. A $230M settlement fund was established for ~600 claimants, effective Dec 2025.
keyTactics: Strategic filing to prevent high-profile depositions.
High 'burn rate' of professional fees to pressure survivors.
Pre-filing asset transfers to shield wealth.

camden.title: Diocese of Camden (NJ)
camden.narrative: Filed Oct 2020. Announced a landmark $180M final resolution. The case involved significant disputes over the valuation of assets and insurance coverage.
keyTactics: Negotiated settlement to avoid 'Corporation Sole' piercing.
Leveraging insurance buyouts.

burlington.title: Diocese of Burlington (VT)
burlington.narrative: Filed Sept 2024 with 118 claims. Reported $35M in central assets, but claimants are targeting $500M in collective parish wealth. Professional fees reached $1.5M in the first year alone.
keyTactics: High professional fee burn rate (5% of assets in year 1).
Shielding parish wealth from the estate.

tucson.title: Diocese of Tucson (AZ)
tucson.narrative: Filed Sept 2004. The second US diocese to file. Settled for $22.2M in 2005.
keyTactics: Early test case for Chapter 11 strategy.

spokane.title: Diocese of Spokane (WA)
spokane.narrative: Filed Dec 2004. Settled for $48M in 2007. A contentious early case.
keyTactics: Aggressive litigation.

portland.title: Archdiocese of Portland (OR)
portland.narrative: Filed July 2004. The very first US diocese to file for bankruptcy on the day a trial was set to begin. Settled for $75M in 2007.
keyTactics: Stopping trial on day of commencement.
Setting the Chapter 11 precedent.

st-paul-minneapolis.title: Archdiocese of St. Paul & Minneapolis (MN)
st-paul-minneapolis.narrative: Filed Jan 2015. Settled for $210M in 2018. A major case that set a high benchmark for settlements.
keyTactics: Large settlement to avoid prolonged litigation.

new-ulm.title: Diocese of New Ulm (MN)
keyTactics: Following the St. Paul precedent.

duluth.title: Diocese of Duluth (MN)
keyTactics: Negotiated settlement.

st-cloud.title: Diocese of St. Cloud (MN)
keyTactics: Delayed filing strategy.

winona-rochester.title: Diocese of Winona-Rochester (MN)
keyTactics: Reorganization and rebranding.

harrisburg.title: Diocese of Harrisburg (PA)
keyTactics: Aggressive asset protection.

greensburg.title: Diocese of Greensburg (PA)
greensburg.narrative: Filed Aug 2020. Resolved through a confidential trust mechanism.
keyTactics: Confidentiality agreements.

great-falls-billings.title: Diocese of Great Falls-Billings (MT)
keyTactics: Quick resolution strategy.

helena.title: Diocese of Helena (MT)
keyTactics: Early adopter of bankruptcy strategy.

fairbanks.title: Diocese of Fairbanks (AK)
fairbanks.narrative: Filed Feb 2008. Settled for $9.8M in 2010. First mission diocese to file.
keyTactics: Pleading mission status poverty.

agana.title: Archdiocese of Agana (GU)
agana.narrative: Filed Jan 2019. Still active. Involves complex international property issues.
keyTactics: International asset shielding.

san-juan.title: Archdiocese of San Juan (PR)
san-juan.narrative: Filed Aug 2018. Case dismissed as the court ruled the Archdiocese was not a legal entity capable of filing bankruptcy under PR law.
keyTactics: Legal entity defense.

wilmington.title: Diocese of Wilmington (DE)
keyTactics: Mid-Atlantic strategy.

norwich.title: Diocese of Norwich (CT)
norwich.narrative: Filed July 2021. Still active. Contentious disputes over insurance.
keyTactics: Insurance litigation.

milwaukee.title: Archdiocese of Milwaukee (WI)
milwaukee.narrative: Filed Jan 2011. Settled for $21M in 2015. Infamous for the 'Cemetery Trust' maneuver.
keyTactics: Cemetery Trust asset shielding.

davenport.title: Diocese of Davenport (IA)
keyTactics: Early Midwest filing.
